about: The kinds of sound in 'Nostromo boot sequence + Interface 2037' (jpcqa, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2ywWFvjE-yU), the film's computer sounds. The user, 2026-09-27: 'this is very good ... it basically contains all the various sounds you'd want, we can inventory all of them separately.' Times in seconds from the start of the video; found from its spectrogram and onsets (scripts/sound-check). For measuring and as models to rebuild our own sounds from, not for use in the shorts. scripts/sound-inventory cuts each into public/local/sfx/reference/boot/ (gitignored) and measures it.

items.name: warble
items.what: two tones taking turns, about 483 and 900 Hz with overtones, about 8 a second; a short 2.6 kHz trill over it at 1.2-2.2 s

items.name: chatter
items.what: dense clicks about 15 a second, noise at 200-800 Hz reaching 6 kHz: a relay bank or teleprinter

items.name: hum-and-beeps
items.what: a loud hum near 110 Hz, with single beeps at 1,233-1,300 Hz

items.name: sweep
items.what: a low tone gliding from under 40 Hz up to about 700 Hz: powering up

items.name: chatter-low
items.what: clicks at 300-400 Hz about 14 a second, with 1-2 kHz ticks: a slower, lower chatter

items.name: mains
items.what: the steady hum band, 30-300 Hz, under the later scenes, with little on top

items.name: wind-down
items.what: regular clicks at about 333 Hz, 16 a second, decaying: a mechanism running down

items.name: carrier
items.what: a held tone at 2,000 Hz with fainter tones near 1.3 and 5 kHz

items.name: pips
items.what: fast pips at 766 Hz, about 13 a second, after a falling 1,650-1,166 Hz figure

items.name: air
items.what: a burst of high noise at 3-4.3 kHz: air or a servo

items.name: high-pips
items.what: pips at 2.6-3 kHz, then noisy chatter at 2.4-2.9 kHz
